notes: §1985:X.5.4.3 SR1: an EXIT PROGRAM in 'a consecutive sequence of imperative statements within a sentence' must 'appear as the last statement in that sequence'. VersionConformancePass.VisitExitStatement asks StatementPosition.Of(stmt).EndsImperativeRun, true when the statement is last or the next one is conditional (an imperative statement includes a delimited scope statement, §1985 IV definition), and otherwise checks the exit-program-not-last-2002 construct, an error COBOL0900 at 85 that 2002 and later admit. Probes at --std 85 in a called program: EXIT PROGRAM DISPLAY, DISPLAY EXIT PROGRAM STOP RUN, EXIT PROGRAM EXIT PROGRAM, and EXIT PROGRAM followed by IF ... END-IF or ADD ... END-ADD are refused COBOL0900, as are the non-last forms inside an IF branch, an ELSE, an inline PERFORM, ON SIZE ERROR and an EVALUATE WHEN; DISPLAY EXIT PROGRAM, EXIT PROGRAM last in IF/ELSE, inline PERFORM and ON SIZE ERROR, EXIT PROGRAM followed by an unterminated IF or ADD ON SIZE ERROR, and EXIT PROGRAM. with a next sentence all return (BACK); the same EXIT PROGRAM DISPLAY runs at 2002 and 2023. Witness: EXIT PROGRAM DISPLAY "AFTER" refused COBOL0900.

next.reason: 1985: "If an EXIT PROGRAM statement appears in a consecutive sequence of imperative statements within a sentence, it must appear as the last"; 2023: "EXIT syntax rules (SR-14.9.14.3-1..10) set no position for EXIT PROGRAM; only GO TO keeps the 'last statement' rule". The 2023 EXIT syntax rules cover EXIT PROGRAM but drop the last-in-sequence requirement. GR-2 even treats EXIT PROGRAM as CONTINUE, so statements after it can run.
